title: Page structure and headings
brief:
A web page is text with tags around it. Tags tell the browser what each part is: a heading, a paragraph, a list.

The page on the right is about a student club, but its structure is wrong: it uses bold text instead of headings, and it has no title. Fix it. The checklist under the preview turns green as you go.

Every page needs exactly one h1 (the main heading). Use h2 for the sections under it.

vocabulary.gloss:
one piece of a page: an opening tag, content, and a closing tag, like

Hello
h1 is the main heading of the page; h2, h3 are smaller headings under it
the name of the page shown on the browser tab; it goes in the <head>, not on the page
what the browser shows for your HTML

starterHtml:
Robotics Club

We meet every Tuesday at 5 pm in room B12. Everyone is welcome, even if you have never built a robot.

What we do

We build small robots, write the code that controls them, and enter a competition in spring.

How to join Come to a meeting, or send an email to the club president.

checks.label: The page has a title (look at the <title> tag in the <head>)
There are at least two h2 headings
There are at least three paragraphs (p)
No more <b> tags are used as headings
